failure_summary.description: Some trajectories omitted a requested operation or subcheck embedded in a compound clause, such as a separate financing lookup or disposable-email check.
Some calls used an endpoint that did not best match the full requested operation, or did not use the exact fully qualified tool name.
Explicit qualifiers were missed, placed in the wrong parameter bucket, or given values inconsistent with the documented schema.
One response duplicated an object key, causing a requested optional parameter to be lost.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already covers exact tool names, schema fidelity, and final-output validation, so repeating those rules is not warranted. Clarifying how to handle compound clauses targets the recurring gap where a call covers only part of a requested outcome or a distinct operation is omitted.

edits.content: - For a clause that requests multiple checks or operations on one target, identify each requested outcome before selecting endpoints. Prefer one endpoint only when its documented output covers the full requested outcome; otherwise, call the best-fitting endpoint for each distinct requested operation or check. Do not treat a broad or narrower partial match as coverage of the whole clause.
